reason: The text demonstrates the Hebrews' foundational relationship with Yahweh through multiple indicators: (1) they obey Yahweh's commands through Moses; (2) they are specifically freed from Egyptian slavery to 'serve Yahweh' (לְכ֛וּ עִבְד֥וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה); (3) Yahweh's divine power and direct intervention are presented as central to their liberation; (4) the entire narrative structure places adherence to Yahweh's will at the center of Hebrew identity and destiny. The exodus itself is framed not merely as political liberation but as enabling religious service to Yahweh.
